[[Jawaharlal Nehru University]] ([[Master of Arts|MA]], [[Master of Philosophy|MPhil]]) | occupation = Politician | profession = | website = {{URL|https://nirmalasitharaman.in/}} }} '''Nirmala Sitharaman''' (born 18 August 1959) is an Indian economist and politician who is serving as the 30th [[Minister of Finance (India)|Minister of Finance]] and 32nd [[Ministry of Corporate Affairs|Minister of Corporate Affairs]] since 2019. She previously served as the [[Minister of Defence (India)|minister of defence]] from 2017 to 2019. A member of the [[Bharatiya Janata Party]] (BJP), she was elected as a [[Member of Parliament (India)|member]] of the [[Rajya Sabha]], the upper house of the [[Parliament of India|Indian Parliament]], from [[List of Rajya Sabha members from Karnataka|Karnataka]] in July 2016. Born in a [[Tamils|Tamil]] family in 1959 at [[Madurai]], Sitharaman obtained her [[Bachelor of Arts]] in Economics from [[Seethalakshmi Ramaswami College]] in 1980, and a [[Master of Arts]] in Economics and [[Master of Philosophy]] from the [[Jawaharlal Nehru University]] in 1984. She briefly worked in various roles in the United Kingdom before returning to India. In 2003, she was appointed as a member of the [[National Commission for Women]] from 2003, and served till 2005. Sitharaman joined the BJP in 2008 and served as a national spokesperson for the party from 2010 to 2014. In May 2014, she was appointed as the [[minister of state]] with an independent charge of the [[Ministry of Commerce and Industry (India)|ministry of commerce and industry]] in the [[first Modi ministry]], and held the position till September 2017. She also held the role of minister of state in the [[Ministry of Finance (India)|finance]] and [[Ministry of Corporate Affairs|corporate affairs]] ministries briefly from May to November 2014. After assuming office, she was elected to the Rajya Sabha from [[List of Rajya Sabha members from Andhra Pradesh|Andhra Pradesh]] in June 2014. On 3 September 2017, she was appointed as the 28th defence minister. On 30 May 2019, Sitharaman was appointed as the minister of finance and corporate affairs in the [[second Modi ministry]]. After serving for five years, she was reappointed to the position in the [[third Modi ministry]] in June 2024, after the [[National Democratic Alliance]] won the [[2024 Indian general election]]. She is the first woman to hold the positions of minister of defence and minister of finance full-time.{{efn|name=Indira|[[Indira Gandhi]], who was the [[Prime Minister of India|Indian prime minister]], held additional responsibilities as the minister of finance in 1970, and the minister of defence from 1980 to 1982.}} In July 2025, she became the longest continuous-serving Indian finance minister, surpassing [[C. D. Deshmukh]]. In February 2026, she became the first Indian finance minister to present the [[Budget of India|union budget]] for nine consecutive times. ==Early life and education== Sitharaman was born into a [[Tamils|Tamil]] [[Iyengar]] family in [[Madurai]], [[Tamil Nadu]], to Savitri and Narayanan Sitharaman.{{cite encyclopedia |last=Chaudhuri |first=Shatarupa |date=24 September 2025|title=Nirmala Sitharaman |url=https://www.britannica.com/money/Nirmala-Sitharaman |access-date=24 September 2025 |encyclopedia=[[Britannica]] }}{{cite web |title=Nirmala Sitharaman Biography: Age, Family, Education, Political Career, Recognitions |url=https://www.jagranjosh.com/general-knowledge/nirmala-sitharaman-1587988863-1 |work=[[Jagranjosh]] |date=1 February 2026 |access-date=1 June 2025}}{{cite web |title=Nirmala Sitharaman |work=[[Ministry of Finance (India)|Ministry of Finance]], [[Government of India]] |url=https://financialservices.gov.in/beta/en/minister/smt-nirmala-sitharaman |access-date=1 June 2025}} Her father worked with the [[Indian Railways]].{{cite web |date=5 July 2019 |title=Nirmala Sitharaman's parents watch her first budget speech in Parliament |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/budget/budget-2019-nirmala-sitharaman-s-parents-watch-her-first-budget-speech-in-parliament/story-FSFYMAS6Q44ooWifF6gESL.html |access-date=1 June 2025 |work=[[The Hindustan Times]]}}{{cite web|url=https://www.deccanherald.com/india/karnatakas-representative-in-union-cabinet-nirmala-sitharaman-3059465|title=Karnataka's representative in Union Cabinet: Nirmala Sitharaman profile|work=[[Deccan Herald]]|date=10 June 2024|access-date=1 June 2025}} She studied at Sacred Heart Convent Anglo-Indian School in [[Viluppuram]] and then at the Vidyodaya School in [[Chennai]]. She has also worked as a senior manager of [[Research and development|R&D]] at [[PricewaterhouseCoopers]] and at the [[BBC World Service]] briefly.{{cite news |date=3 September 2017 |title=In Nirmala Sitharaman, India Gets Its Second Woman Defence Minister After Indira Gandhi |url=http://www.huffingtonpost.in/2017/09/03/in-nirmala-sitharaman-india-gets-its-second-woman-defence-minis_a_23195198/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170913183454/http://www.huffingtonpost.in/2017/09/03/in-nirmala-sitharaman-india-gets-its-second-woman-defence-minis_a_23195198/ |archive-date=13 September 2017 |access-date=13 September 2017 |work=[[Huffington Post]]}} After returning to India in 1991, she served as the deputy director of the Centre for Public Policy Studies in [[Hyderabad]]. In 2004, she was one of the founding directors of Pranava, a private [[co-educational school]] in Hyderabad.{{cite web |last=Menon |first=Amarnath K. |date=5 September 2017 |title=Nirmala Sitharaman's rise from activist to Defence Minister |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/india/delhi/story/nirmala-sitharaman-defence-minister-cabinet-reshuffle-sushma-swaraj-1038180-2017-09-05 |access-date=24 September 2025 |work=[[India Today]] }} She was appointed as a member of the [[National Commission for Women]] in 2003, and served in the position till 2005.{{cite news |title=Nirmala Sitharaman and the Budget: A lady's day out |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/magazines/panache/nirmala-sitharaman-and-the-budget-a-ladys-day-out/articleshow/73803594.cms |work=[[The Economic Times]] |date=1 February 2020 |access-date=10 June 2024 |archive-date=10 June 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240610180917/https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/magazines/panache/nirmala-sitharaman-and-the-budget-a-ladys-day-out/articleshow/73803594.cms |url-status=live }} ==Political career== Sitharaman joined the [[Bharatiya Janata Party]] (BJP) in 2006 and was appointed to its national executive committee in 2008. Nirmala Sitharaman (born 18 August 1959) is an Indian economist and politician who is serving as the 30th Minister of Finance and 32nd Minister of Corporate Affairs since 2019. She previously served as the minister of defence from 2017 to 2019. A member of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), she was elected as a member of the Rajya Sabha, the upper house of the Indian Parliament, from Karnataka in July 2016.
Born in a Tamil family in 1959 at Madurai, Sitharaman obtained her Bachelor of Arts in Economics from Seethalakshmi Ramaswami College in 1980, and a Master of Arts in Economics and Master of Philosophy from the Jawaharlal Nehru University in 1984. She briefly worked in various roles in the United Kingdom before returning to India. In 2003, she was appointed as a member of the National Commission for Women from 2003, and served till 2005.
Sitharaman joined the BJP in 2008 and served as a national spokesperson for the party from 2010 to 2014. In May 2014, she was appointed as the minister of state with an independent charge of the ministry of commerce and industry in the first Modi ministry, and held the position till September 2017. She also held the role of minister of state in the finance and corporate affairs ministries briefly from May to November 2014. After assuming office, she was elected to the Rajya Sabha from Andhra Pradesh in June 2014. On 3 September 2017, she was appointed as the 28th defence minister.
On 30 May 2019, Sitharaman was appointed as the minister of finance and corporate affairs in the second Modi ministry. After serving for five years, she was reappointed to the position in the third Modi ministry in June 2024, after the National Democratic Alliance won the 2024 Indian general election. She is the first woman to hold the positions of minister of defence and minister of finance full-time. In July 2025, she became the longest continuous-serving Indian finance minister, surpassing C. D. Deshmukh. In February 2026, she became the first Indian finance minister to present the union budget for nine consecutive times.
